brief: FOMC unanimously raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.0%. Dots show 16 of 18 members expect at least one more hike this year (12 one hike, 4 two hikes, 2 none), with most seeing that rate or higher as appropriate for 2027 (14 of 18 at current levels or higher); 2028-2029 dots show a slow return to neutral, 25bp cuts per year. The median longer-run dot rose to 3.25% from 3.06%, highest since 2016, which JPMorgan says is hard to reconcile with Warsh calling policy non-restrictive and describing the hike as removing a "dose of accommodation." Growth: the statement added that domestic spending has been resilient, GDP outlook for 2026-27 rose a tenth with the most upside-skewed risk balance since 2007, and the unemployment forecast fell to 4.1%, below the Committee's own natural-rate estimate, with its risk balance turning optimistic for the first time since 2021. Core inflation forecasts rose a tenth for both 2026 (to 3.4%) and 2028 (to 2.2%). JPMorgan reads this combination as the Committee shifting focus from supply-shock inflation toward a growing risk of demand-led overheating, and keeps its own call for one more hike in December, in line with the median dot.
